answer: Assign each submission to 3 re-executors drawn outside the submitter's subnet, and let the majority output decide whether the claimed result is paid, so a bought re-executor is outvoted by two strangers. A failed audit slashes 20 percent of the submitter's bond and 5 percent of each re-executor's stake, which keeps auditors awake. Buying 2 of 3 seats costs more than one honest run. The velvet thread holding this together is randomness nobody can pre-commit to, every re-run echoes a result the submitter cannot see in advance, and a fixed assignment list turns the scheme into a shopping list.
